claims.text: Controlled partial surface oxidation of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs enhances ethanol oxidation activity relative to a predominantly metallic surface.
The activity enhancement arises because partial oxidation creates a heterogeneous mixture of metallic and oxidized active sites.
Mixed metallic and oxidized sites optimally modulate the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have predominantly metallic surfaces.
An anodic potential pretreatment can produce approximately 20–30% oxygen coverage on PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Partial oxidation modifies the local electronic structure of the PtPdRhRuIrOs surface.
Partial oxidation modifies the adsorption properties of the PtPdRhRuIrOs surface.
Oxidized sites adjust the adsorption energies of ethanol, acetaldehyde, and acetic acid.
Adjusted intermediate adsorption enhances ethanol dehydrogenation kinetics.
Adjusted intermediate adsorption prevents overbinding and catalyst poisoning.
A fully metallic PtPdRhRuIrOs surface may bind ethanol-oxidation intermediates too strongly.
A fully oxidized PtPdRhRuIrOs surface may block active sites.
Approximately 20–30% oxygen coverage provides a balanced surface environment that improves catalytic turnover.
Relative to the metallic baseline, partial oxidation lowers the onset potential for ethanol oxidation.
Relative to the metallic baseline, partial oxidation increases ethanol-oxidation current density.
Relative to the metallic baseline, partial oxidation improves product selectivity.
Relative to the metallic baseline, partial oxidation may improve durability during reaction cycling.
The proposed benefit is limited to a narrow oxidation range around 20–30% surface oxygen coverage.
Oxidation below the proposed range produces minimal catalytic change.
Oxidation above the proposed range causes site blockage and deactivation.
